body:
# Tasks — Inventory + Gap Analysis

Snapshot of everything filemark's task system actually has, benchmarked against the class of markdown task tools, with a ranked list of gaps worth closing vs. YAGNI items to skip. Written for two audiences: (1) future AI sessions that need a one-doc summary of the feature surface without reading every phase of `TASKS_PLAN.md`, and (2) humans deciding what to build next.

- **Date opened:** 2026-04-24
- **Companion docs:** `docsi/TASKS_PLAN.md` (the canonical spec), `docsi/THEMING.md` (CSS/theme contract)
- **Coverage as of this doc:** Phases 1–5.5 shipped; Phase 6 explicitly skipped.

---

## 1. Feature inventory — what's shipped

### 1.1 Grammar / parser (Phase 1)

- **6 statuses** — `[ ]` todo, `[/]` wip, `[x]` done, `[!]` blocked, `[?]` question, `[-]` cancelled
- **14 metadata sigils** — `@owner`, `!p0..p3` (+ `!high`/`!med`/`!low` aliases), `~due`, `^start`, `#tag`, `(project)`, `&estimate`, `$cost`, `%percent`, `.area`, `*goal`, `+created`, `=completed`, `every:<spec>`, `x-<field>=<value>`
- **7 dependency relations** — `after:`, `before:`, `blocks:`, `requires:`, `parent:`, `children:`, `related:` (all parse; `after` / `requires` / `parent` additionally drive `is:blocked` / `is:unblocked`)
- **7 link shortcodes** — `gh:`, `linear:`, `jira:`, `slack:`, `notion:`, `figma:`, `yt:` — expand via registry to full URLs with typed metadata (org/repo/number for GitHub, etc.)
- **URL auto-detection** for bare `https://…` (github.com/*/pull, github.com/*/issues, linear.app, atlassian.net, slack.com, notion.so, figma.com, youtube.com)
- **Markdown links** `[label](url)` preserved in text and classified as TaskLinks
- **Three escape mechanisms** — tail-scan (default), `::` explicit metadata fence, `\` backslash on individual sigil chars, `` `inline code` `` always literal
- **11 recurrence forms** — `daily`, `weekly`, `biweekly`, `monthly`, `quarterly`, `yearly` / `annually`, `mon,wed,fri` (weekday sets), `Nweeks`, `Nd` (every-N), `first-<day>`, `last-<day>`
- **Rich time expressions** — ISO dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`), ISO weeks/months/quarters, keywords (`today`, `tomorrow`, `eow`, `eom`, `eoq`, `eoy`, weekday names), relative offsets (`+3d`, `+2w`, `-7d`), ranges (`start..end`)
- **Cascading defaults** — task-line > fence info-string > frontmatter > global
- **Round-trip serializer** — `parse(line) → serialize(task) → parse(line)` is byte-identical for canonical inputs; enables AI agents to edit a single line without clobbering formatting
- **Auto-ids** via FNV-1a hash of `file:line:text:status`; **stable ids** via `^task-<slug>` suffix
- **Diagnostics** — `unknown-sigil`, `bad-date`, `unknown-priority`, `orphan-ref`, `duplicate-id`, `ambiguous-tail`, `type-mismatch`, `circular-dep`, `unknown-shortcode`, `unknown-owner` (rendered as ⚠ chip with hover-tooltip)

### 1.2 Rich task detail (Phase 5.5)

- **`Task.detail`** — raw markdown source slice of any indented block content below a bullet (paragraphs / images / code fences / tables / callouts / embedded components)
- **`Task.detailLineRange`** — `[startLine, endLine]` for "jump to source"
- **`TaskDetailSheet`** — portal-rendered right-side drawer (~560px); backdrop + slide-in; closes on X / Escape / backdrop click; scroll-lock on body while open
- **Full component parity inside detail** — the sheet renders through the same remark-gfm + remark-math + remark-breaks + remarkCodeMeta + rehype-raw + rehype-slug + rehype-katex pipeline and the same components map as the main viewer, so `<Chart>`, `<Kanban md>`, `<Stats>`, nested `<TaskList>` / `<TaskStats>` / `<TaskTimeline>`, `<ADR>`, `<Callout>`, `<Details>`, `<Tabs>`, images via `SmartImage`, links via `SmartLink`, code via `CodeBlock` all work
- **Nested task detail** — each subtask is an independent `Task` with its own `detail` + independent sheet; rich detail works recursively
- **📎 detail chip surfaces** — inline `<li>` (TaskItem), `<TaskList>` rows, `<Kanban md>` cards, and chrome-ext TaskPanel rows all show a `📎 detail` chip when `task.detail` is non-empty; clicking opens the sheet

### 1.3 Views

**In-doc components (Phases 2–3):**

- **Enhanced `<li>` TaskItem** — every `- [ ]` bullet in any markdown doc renders with status icon + metadata chips + blocked-by resolution + detail chip
- **`<TaskList>`** — grouped list; `filter=` / `group-by=` / `sort=` / `limit=` / `order=` / `title=` / `empty=`; reuses same chip family
- **`<TaskStats md>`** — 8 KPI tiles built on top of the shipped `<Stats>` / `<Stat>` primitives (total / todo / wip / blocked / done / overdue / today / this-week)
- **`<Kanban md>`** — task-source board; `group-by=` any of status/owner/priority/project/file/due-bucket/tag; `order=` explicit column pinning; column-key chip dedup (don't repeat the groupKey on each card); own lightweight Column/Card — separate from `@filemark/kanban`'s CSV-driven internals
- **`<TaskTimeline md>`** — pure-SVG Gantt-lite; 3 bar shapes (rectangle for `^start..~due`, diamond for due-only, open arrow for start-only); today dashed marker; priority colors; lane grouping; vertical scroll when rows exceed container

**App-level surface (Phase 4):**

- **`<TaskPanel>`** in `apps/chrome-ext` — right-edge ~380px side dashboard; 6 filter tabs (All · Open · Today · This week · Overdue · Blocked); search box; group-by chooser; click-to-scroll with blue flash highlight on target row; ⌘T shortcut + TopBar toggle + UIPrefs persistence

### 1.4 Query DSL (Phase 2)

- **Comparison** — `status=todo`, `priority<=p1`, `due<=today`, `estimate>2h`, `percent>=50`
- **Set membership** — `owner in (alice,bob)`, `tag in (grid,v2)`, `status not in (done,cancelled)`
- **Boolean combinators** — `AND`, `OR`, `NOT` with parens
- **Existential** — `has:due`, `has:estimate`, `has:pr`, `has:x-<field>`, `missing:due`, `missing:owner`
- **Derived predicates** — `is:overdue`, `is:today`, `is:tomorrow`, `is:upcoming`, `is:unblocked`, `is:blocked`, `is:recurring`, `is:done`, `is:open`
- **Text search** — `text:"substring"`, `contains:"..."`, `mentions:@alice`
- **Link filters** — `linked:pr`, `linked:issue`, `linked:linear`, `linked:gh:*/*#*` (glob)
- **Dependency filters** — `after:task-id`, `parent:task-id`, `blocks:any`
- **Hand-rolled recursive-descent parser** → AST → evaluator. No `eval()`; safe against untrusted predicate strings.

### 1.5 Group + sort (Phase 2)

- **14 group keys** — status, owner, tag, priority, project, area, goal, file, depth, due-day, due-week, due-month, due-quarter, due-bucket, created-day, created-week
- **`due-bucket` smart grouper** — Overdue → Today → Tomorrow → This week → Next week → Later → No due (ordered render)
- **Multi-key sort** via `parseSortSpec` → `"priority:asc,due:asc,text:asc"`
- **Many-to-many groups** — tasks with multiple owners / tags appear in each matching group

### 1.6 Cross-file aggregation (Phase 4)

- **`useTaskIndex`** Zustand store in `apps/chrome-ext` — content-hash-keyed parsed task cache
- **Body-relative line numbers** — aligned with react-markdown's DOM so click-to-source hits the right `<li data-fv-task-line="…">` anchor
- **`resolveBlockers(task, universe)`** exported from `@filemark/tasks` — walks `after:` / `requires:` / `parent:` refs across every task in scope
- **Dependency-aware predicates** — `is:blocked` / `is:unblocked` check actual prerequisite status rather than just dep-array length
- **Scroll-to-source with flash** — `scrollTarget` state + `rev` counter for re-triggering + poll-until-element-mounts (up to 2s) + `fv-task-flash` transient highlight

### 1.7 Grep-friendliness (Phase 1 invariant)

- **One task = one line** — hard invariant; no line continuation; multi-line content goes in child sub-bullets (notes) or indented blocks (detail)
- **ASCII sigils only** — no Unicode; cross-platform regex-safe
- **ISO dates** — `YYYY-MM-DD` canonical; keywords limited to small enumerable set
- **Identifier-safe payloads** — `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` for owners, tags, project names; no quotes, no embedded spaces
- **Space-delimited tokens** — `\s+` always splits cleanly
- **10+ documented grep patterns** catalogued in `docsi/TASKS_PLAN.md §6.7`

### 1.8 Theming (the package-CSS refactor)

- **~55 `--fm-*` CSS variables** covering semantic tones (success / warn / danger / info / owner / muted / project), chip geometry, prose typography, table density, callout borders, timeline bars, kanban columns, ADR padding, task-flash highlight, detail sheet
- **`@filemark/mdx/styles.css`** — single CSS file shipped with the package via `package.json#exports`; imported once in each app's `main.tsx`; zero duplication between chrome-ext and playground
- **Fallbacks at usage sites** — every `var(--fm-X, fallback)` defaults either to a shadcn token (`var(--destructive)`, `var(--primary)`) or to a literal; no `:root` block in packages → no drift
- **Shadcn-combobox theme switcher** built on `@base-ui/react/combobox` — searchable, keyboard-navigable, grouped by category (Built-in / Demo / Custom), each theme shows label + description
- **Sample themes** — Neon (violet canvas, magenta chips, square corners, Inter prose) + Solarized (paper base, muted teal, serif prose)
- **Theme registration contract** — a theme is a CSS file with `html[data-theme="<name>"] { --fm-*: ...; }`; add to `THEMES` registry, import the CSS once, users pick from the dropdown; no component rebuild ever needed

### 1.9 AI-friendliness (Phase 1 design principle)

- **Simple positional rule** — "put metadata at the end; stop when you want"
- **Non-overlapping ASCII sigils** — each sigil has one meaning
- **Standard markdown primitives reused** — GFM task bullets, markdown links, inline code literals
- **Round-trip safety** — `parse → modify → serialize` never clobbers untouched tokens; safe programmatic edits
- **Predicate DSL as NL-translation target** — LLM translates "show overdue p0 for alice" → `is:overdue AND priority=p0 AND owner=alice`
- **Typed values** — Priority enum, TimeValue, Duration, Money, percent — not stringly-typed
- **Cascading defaults** — shorter AI output (frontmatter `default-owner: alice` means every task doesn't need `@alice`)
- **Explicit diagnostics** — parser warnings with position + hint enable AI self-correction in tool-use loops

### 1.10 Other (pre-task infrastructure reused)

- **`<Stats>` / `<Stat>`** primitives (underpins `<TaskStats md>`)
- **`<Kanban src=…>`** CSV-source kanban (Phase 3 of kanban feature; separate from `<Kanban md>`)
- **TaskCheckbox** persistence via `StorageAdapter` (predates the Tasks DSL)
- **`SmartImage` / `SmartLink`** for asset resolution + link classification
- **Shiki syntax highlighting** for code fences
- **KaTeX** math rendering inside task detail

---

## 2. Benchmark — filemark vs. the class

| Feature | Filemark | Obsidian Tasks | Logseq | Notion | Linear |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reader-first / own your data | ✅ | ⚠ editor-bound | ⚠ editor-bound | ❌ SaaS | ❌ SaaS |
| Markdown as source of truth | ✅ | ✅ | ⚠ (own block format) | ❌ | ❌ |
| AI-editable (round-trip safe grammar) | ✅ | ⚠ (partially) | ⚠ | ⚠ (via API) | ⚠ (via API) |
| Multiple views from one source | ✅ list/board/stats/timeline | ⚠ partial | ⚠ partial | ✅ | ✅ |
| Rich detail with embedded components | ✅ full | ❌ | ⚠ blocks | ✅ | ⚠ |
| Cross-file aggregation | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Dependency graph (predicate-aware) | ⚠ parsed + resolveBlockers; no graph view | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Recurrence | ✅ 11 forms | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Grep-friendly | ✅ full | ✅ | ⚠ | ❌ | ❌ |
| Theming (~50+ tokens) | ✅ | ⚠ (Obsidian themes) | ⚠ | ⚠ partial | ❌ |
| Local-only / offline | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| Zero lock-in | ✅ | ⚠ (Obsidian-specific emoji syntax) | ⚠ (own block format) | ❌ | ❌ |
| No subscription / no account | ✅ | ⚠ (Obsidian Sync paid) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| Embed charts / kanban / stats inside a task | ✅ (unique) | ❌ | ❌ | ⚠ (blocks) | ❌ |
| Task IDs stable across moves | ✅ (`^task-slug`) | ⚠ (emoji-based) | ✅ (block ids) | ✅ | ✅ |

**Empty quadrant filemark owns:** reader-first + markdown-native + multi-view + AI-editable + zero-lock-in + embed-components-inside-tasks.

---

## 3. Gap analysis — what's worth adding vs. skipping

### 3.1 Tier A — high value, small scope (half to one day each)

Each of these sharpens ergonomics without adding new capability classes. Collectively they take filemark from "feature-complete" to "comfortable daily driver."

1. **Keyboard navigation** in TaskPanel + TaskList — `j` / `k` to move between rows, `Space` to toggle check, `/` to focus search, `Enter` to open detail sheet, `Esc` to close. Linear-style ergonomics.
2. **Collapse-all / Expand-all** toggle — one button in the TopBar when the active doc has ≥ 3 tasks with details. Useful for "scan the list" vs "read the whole plan."
3. **Quick-filter chips** — click any chip in any view (owner, tag, project, priority) → that value becomes an added filter predicate in the TaskList / Kanban / panel. One-click drill-down.
4. **Search highlighting** in TaskPanel — the substring match should bold/highlight the matched text in each row, not just filter.
5. **Overdue badge on TaskPanel TopBar icon** — small count indicator on the `ListTodo` button showing `is:overdue` count across all opened files.
6. **Status-menu on click** — click a status glyph / checkbox → small popover with the 6 statuses (todo / wip / done / blocked / question / cancelled) to change without editing markdown. **Caveat:** requires a decision on write-back (see Tier C #1).
7. **Copy task ref** — right-click a task → "Copy ^task-slug" generates a stable id (auto-promotes if currently auto-hashed) and copies to clipboard. Cheap, surprisingly useful for cross-references.

### 3.2 Tier B — useful but heavier (1 day each)

Visual features that differentiate filemark more clearly but aren't necessary for daily use.

1. **`<TaskDepGraph md>`** — SVG graph of the dependency DAG. Nodes = tasks, edges = `after:` / `requires:` / `parent:` refs. Useful for "what's blocking what" visualization. Reuse force-directed layout from a small lib or hand-roll.
2. **`<TaskHeatmap md>`** — GitHub-style activity calendar keyed by `=completed` dates. Visual momentum indicator; nice for "am I shipping regularly?"
3. **`<TaskBurndown md>`** for a filtered slice (e.g., a sprint doc) — remaining vs. time chart using `=completed` dates.
4. **`<TaskCalendar md>`** — month-grid view keyed by `~due` / `^start`. Clicking a day opens a mini drawer with tasks on that day. (Originally planned for Phase 5; deferred.)
5. **Saved filters / bookmarks** — persist named filter+group+sort combos in UIPrefs so you can switch between "Today's work" / "Overdue" / "P0 backlog" without retyping.
6. **Active-task pinning** — pin specific tasks to the top of the panel regardless of filter. For current in-flight work.

### 3.3 Tier C — significant new capability or open question

1. **Write-back on toggle / edit** — the big open question. Filemark is reader-first, which is a real virtue (no format lock-in, AI can edit the file directly, files open in any editor). But `StorageAdapter` tick state is per-machine and invisible to anything else. Decision fork:
    - **Stay reader-first:** AI or user edits the markdown; we auto-refresh. Status-menu (Tier A #6) would go through the AI or a small `fs.writeFile` adapter behind a feature flag.
    - **Add opt-in write-back:** a settings toggle "write task changes to markdown." When on, ticking `[ ]` → `[x]` rewrites the file line in place. Gated behind FSA write permission.
    - **Ship both:** read-only default; power-users enable write-back. This is probably the right path long-term but doubles the surface area.
2. **`{k:v}` dense-block form** (from Phase 1 grammar spec) — `- [ ] Ship v2 {owner: alice, priority: p0, due: 2026-04-28}` alternative to sigils. Never shipped. Minor; sigil form covers all cases. Keep as design note.
3. **Natural-language filter box** — "overdue p0 for alice" → predicate DSL via LLM. Requires AI integration.
4. **`@ai:<action>` markers** — render a ✨ button on tasks like `- [ ] research @ai:summarize`; clicking runs an LLM call with task + refs as context and appends a sub-bullet. Requires configured API key + cost disclaimers.
5. **Semantic dedup detector** — flag near-identical tasks via embedding similarity. AI dep; not needed at ~1000-task scale.
6. **Import/export adapters** — Obsidian Tasks / Logseq / Todo.txt importers; iCal / CSV / JSON-LD exporters; GitHub Issues bridge. Only worth building when someone actually has data stuck in those formats.
7. **`filemark tasks <sub>` CLI** — grep / show / format / stats / graph / lint / validate. Deferred Phase 6. TaskPanel + shell `grep -r` cover the interactive case; CLI adds most value alongside import/export.

### 3.4 YAGNI — deliberately skipping

Decisions already locked in `TASKS_PLAN.md §2` and reinforced here. Don't revisit unless the premise fundamentally shifts.

- **Real-time multi-user sync** — would require a server + auth + conflict resolution. Kills reader-first identity. Different product.
- **LSP / IDE integrations** — niche audience; grammar is simple enough that users don't need autocomplete.
- **Server-backed storage** — defeats the "your markdown is the database" thesis.
- **RRULE-style recurrence engine** — current 11 forms cover practical use. No need for VEVENT-grade calendar math.
- **Gantt critical-path highlighting** — cool but niche. Timeline + dependency chip is enough context.
- **Task comments / discussion threads** — use GitHub PRs, email, Slack. Filemark isn't a collab platform.
- **Attachments / file uploads** — markdown already has `![](path)` and `[label](path)`. No need for a custom attachments model.
- **Notifications / push** — no server, no push.

---

## 4. "Best markdown task system" scorecard

How does filemark stack up on the definitional features of a best-in-class markdown task system?

| Criterion | Status |
|---|---|
| Simple, composable DSL | ✅ 14 sigils, ASCII, space-delimited, tail-scan + `::` + `\` escapes |
| Grep-friendly by invariant | ✅ one task = one line; ISO dates; identifier-safe payloads |
| AI-editable with round-trip safety | ✅ byte-stable parse/serialize |
| Multiple views (list / board / stats / timeline) from one data source | ✅ all four shipped |
| Rich detail (images / code / tables / embedded components) | ✅ with popup sheet |
| Dependency tracking | ✅ parsed + predicate-aware; graph view pending |
| Recurrence | ✅ 11 forms |
| Cross-file aggregation + click-to-source | ✅ TaskPanel + scrollTarget |
| Themable (no hardcoded colors) | ✅ ~55 tokens |
| Reader-first / no format lock-in | ✅ core identity |
| Works offline / no account | ✅ Chrome ext + playground; zero backend |
| Plays nicely with other tools (GitHub / Obsidian renderers) | ✅ standard GFM bullets; metadata renders as literal text in other tools |

**Every definitional feature is shipped.** The polish list (§3.1) determines whether it *feels* like a world-class tool when used daily. Building Tier A is the remaining distance between "functionally complete" and "delightful."

---

## 5. Recommended next steps

Ordered by ROI:

1. **Ship Tier A (§3.1).** Half to one day each; ~3–5 days total; takes filemark to "daily driver" ergonomics. Items 1 (keyboard), 2 (collapse-all), 3 (quick-filter), 4 (search highlight), 5 (overdue badge), 7 (copy task ref). Skip item 6 (status menu) until the write-back question (§3.3 #1) is answered.
2. **Decide on write-back (§3.3 #1).** Biggest open architectural question. Pick one: stay reader-first (cleanest), add opt-in write-back (most flexible), or ship both paths (widest audience). Documenting the decision is more important than implementing it — future AI sessions need to know the answer to avoid re-litigating.
3. **Ship one Tier B item as a flagship demo (§3.2).** DepGraph or Calendar. Good for a marketing screenshot / differentiator; showcases the "one source, many views" thesis at its strongest.
4. **Leave Tier C unbuilt.** Every item in C is either a big scope commitment (AI markers, import/export adapters, CLI) or a deep open question (write-back). Revisit only when a concrete user story demands it.
